videos.description:

videos.title: Nvidia In Crisis: The Rise Of Jensen Huang’s Empire At The Center Of The AI Boom
videos.description:
Nvidia is facing the biggest crisis in its 33 year history, with founder Jensen Huang resigning as CEO Thursday after admitting to having an affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, and accusations of two more affairs with employees inside his company. Now CFO Colette Kress has taken the helm as Nvidia’s interim CEO.

The implications of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang run far deeper than infidelity because her ties to Nvidia customer Megaspeed put her in the middle of a sprawling effort to accumulate AI chips across Southeast Asia. And Megaspeed is under investigation for possibly diverting restricted Nvidia chips into the hands of Chinese companies.

The relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang dates back to 2023, according to The New York Times. It was a “turbulent” time for Nvidia, Jensen Huang told CNBC during an interview at the time, as the company navigated the first in a series of strict export controls the Biden administration placed on sending its most advanced chips to China.

On that same day we interviewed Jensen Huang in 2023, we also interviewed Huang’s direct report Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, with whom Jensen Huang is accused of having an affair.

Three years later, the long-time Nvidia CEO and founder has resigned, and CNBC takes a look back at our interviews with Jensen Huang and other Nvidia executives to get a clear picture of where Nvidia stands today, and all it stands to lose.

U.S. voters passed 40 ballot measures putting limits on AI data centers this week, as huge 1GW AI data centers from OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Amazon, Google and more push up water and power bills and put a strain on local resources. One of the issues that continues to come up is water usage, which is needed to cool the GPUs inside data centers running AI workloads. Closed-loop liquid cooling keeps water use low inside many modern AI data centers, but external cooling is still needed to move heat outside of the buildings and that requires large amounts of power or water in hot climates. CNBC visited data centers and spoke to researchers to find out the truth about how data centers use water.

videos.title: The 'Socialist' Bank Thriving In Trump Country
videos.description:
Progressive political candidates have clamored to launch public banks in the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections. However, there is just one active example in the United States: the Bank of North Dakota. Chartered in 1919, this bank uses tax revenue from the state to fund and execute strategic economic development priorities for North Dakota. The bank has assisted in sales of fossil fuel assets, a presidential library, and general lending to citizens and businesses in need. CNBC's Garrett Downs reports on this “socialist experiment” unfolding deep in Trump country.
